newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA BOLIVAR ENDS FIRM ON CURRENCY SALES.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA BOLIVAR ENDS FIRM ON CURRENCY SALES.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed slightly firmer 494.00/495.00 per dollar Thursday on heavier interbank and Central Bank foreign currency sales, traders said.
The bolivar closed at 494.50/495.50 per dollar Wednesday.
"The market was fairly quiet. The exchange rate fell due to some interbank and Central Bank dollar sales," one trader said.
After depreciating two percent in July the bolivar has rallied in recent days following a series of monetary and currency policy adjustments by the Central Bank.

The Central Bank Monday said it was raising commercial banks' reserve requirement by two percentage points to 17 percent and cutting the depreciation rate of its currency bands system to 1.16 percent per month.
The Bank also clamped down on interbank currency trading by reclassifying a number of institutions previously listed as final clients.
Traders said the measures had reduced currency volatility and given the Central Bank more control over the currency market.
Traders expected the exchange rate to remain broadly flat Friday in relatively quiet trade.
